correctness.rationale: For each prime p≥5, Bang–Zsigmondy supplies a prime q of multiplicative order p−1, no exceptional case applicable. This implies q>p and p−1|q−1; both exact semiprime congruences follow from the order identity and Fermat. The smaller prime p uniquely identifies its product, and pq<p^p combined with the prime number theorem yields the explicit liminf at least one. Every logical step and boundary is verified in RESULT.md. A reproducible exact certificate independently checks seven examples and 23,313 finite semiprimes; finite computations are not used for infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Applying classical Zsigmondy with exponent p-1 yields ord_q(p)=p-1; then p-1 divides q-1 and q is larger than p. These extra deductions meet both necessary congruences from the existing characterization. Thus neither the primitive divisor theorem alone nor the semiprime criterion alone states the full result; their explicit interaction yields the conclusion. No dominance or equivalent theorem was found, not proof of uniqueness.
